title: Opposite interval mapping object exchanges endpoints
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products, internal functor simplicial sets and endpoint evaluations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ put $\theta^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=n-\theta(m-j)$; define $K^{\mathrm{op}}_m=K_m$ with operator $K^{\mathrm{op}}(\theta)=K(\theta^{\mathrm{rev}})$. Put $I=\Delta^1$. For every small simplicial set $E$ the formula
$$R_{E,n}(\alpha)_m(i,\theta)=\alpha_m(i^{\mathrm{rev}},\theta^{\mathrm{rev}}),\qquad \alpha:I\times\Delta^n\to E,$$
where $i:[m]\to[1]$ and $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, defines a natural simplicial isomorphism
$$R_E:\operatorname{Fun}(I,E)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fun}(I,E^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
It satisfies $\operatorname{ev}_a R_E=(\operatorname{ev}_{1-a})^{\mathrm{op}}$ for $a=0,1$, as maps to $E^{\mathrm{op}}$. For every simplicial map $p:E\to B$ it satisfies $R_B\operatorname{Fun}(I,p)^{\mathrm{op}}=\operatorname{Fun}(I,p^{\mathrm{op}})R_E$. The opposite of a degreewise pullback is the pullback of the opposite maps. Thus these identifications carry the opposite of $\rho_0(p)$ to $\rho_1(p^{\mathrm{op}})$, where
$$\rho_a(p):\operatorname{Fun}(I,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_a,B}E,\qquad \alpha\mapsto(p\alpha,\alpha(a)).$$
No Kan condition is imposed on $E$ or $B$.
